text:
Moritz Seider was third of 215 defensemen in Evolving-Hockey's wins above replacement last season, in the 99th percentile for taking chances away. This season he's carrying a heavier load than ever, almost 26 minutes a night, on a team that won't name a captain while Dylan Larkin sits out waiting for a trade. The Detroit Free Press calls him an "all in" guy, and his postgame frustration has been a headline of its own.

The numbers show the strain. Detroit has 49% of the expected goals at five on five with Seider on, five points worse than without him, and he has one goal and 11 points. His shooting is low (2.6%), but the bigger issue is the team in front of him.

He's 25, a Calder winner, and the player the franchise is built around now. Our range has him at 44 to 67 points, but the real measure is whether Detroit's chances turn around with him on the ice.
